title: GTO preflop ranges
description: Six questions on opening, 3-betting, and sizing decisions preflop.

questions.prompt: In a 6-max game, the player who acts first preflop after the cards are dealt sits in which seat?
questions.explanation: In 6-max, the order is LJ → HJ → CO → BTN → SB → BB. LJ acts first preflop (after blinds are posted).

questions.prompt: Approximately what fraction of hands does a solver-derived BTN RFI range play in 6-max at 100bb?
questions.explanation: Modern solver BTN RFI sits around 43–48% — the BTN's positional advantage justifies a wide range. UTG is the tightest, around 10–12% in full ring.

questions.prompt: Default 3-bet sizing when you are out of position is roughly:
questions.explanation: Standard guidance: 3× IP, 4× OOP. The larger OOP size charges callers more, compensating for the positional disadvantage.

questions.prompt: Which range construction is most appropriate when 3-betting against microstakes calling stations?

choices.text: Polarised — mixing premiums with bluffs like A5s.
Linear / merged — TT+, AQo+, AJs+, KQs only.
Limp behind to keep the pot small.
3-bet 100% of hands to maximise fold equity.

questions.explanation: Stations don't fold to 3-bets often enough for bluff combos to be +EV. Use a merged range of value hands that simply want to play a bigger pot as a favourite.

questions.prompt: Modern solver play from the SB is mostly raise-or-fold; flatting an open from the BTN is rarely the best option.
questions.explanation: Calling from the SB leaves you OOP vs the BB with a capped range. Solver outputs almost always prefer a raise-or-fold strategy from the SB, with 3-bets going wide.

questions.prompt: You are in the CO. Which of the following are valid reasons to size your open above 2.5bb?

choices.text: There are two limpers in front of you.
The BB is a calling station who pays off thin value.
The BTN is a tight reg who only calls premiums.
You picked up the table average's tightest 3-bet stat.

questions.explanation: Add ~1bb per limper to charge them, and size up against stations to extract value. Tight BTN regs don't justify a larger size — if anything, they justify smaller opens to steal cheaply.
